description: Welcome to Cosmic Sandbox! We are creating an interactive Space Mission Design Game where players experiment with spacecraft builds, calculate trajectories, and explore distant planets and moons. We are looking for enthusiastic teammates with skills in game development, coding, graphic design, or space science to help us build a fun, hands-on prototype. Join us to turn space exploration into a playable sandbox adventure!
summary:
Project Cosmic Sandbox is an interactive, browser-based 2D space mission design game built with HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript. Powered by real planetary metrics from the NASA Planetary Fact Sheet, the game challenges players to design, balance, and launch spacecraft across five distinct planetary environments and three stellar classes.

To address the Space Mission Design Game challenge, Cosmic Sandbox simulates the real engineering trade-offs behind space exploration. Players select a target world and spacecraft hull—from lightweight CubeSats to heavy flagships—and equip critical subsystems like high-gain antennas, solar arrays, radioisotope power sources, and radiation shielding. Every component affects mass, power generation, and mission budget, forcing players to solve authentic constraints such as extreme temperatures, deep gravity wells, and inverse-square solar power drop-offs before launching into a 2D orbital simulation.

Cosmic Sandbox is important because it transforms complex aerospace engineering into an accessible, hands-on learning tool, inspiring students to understand how NASA engineers turn ambitious space concepts into successful missions.
details:
What It Does & How It Works
Project Cosmic Sandbox is an interactive 2D space mission design game where players act as aerospace systems engineers. Players start by selecting a target planetary system from three star classes (Red, Yellow, and Blue stars) and five planetary profiles (Rocky Planet, Terrestrial Planet, Ice Planet, Ice Giant, and Gas Giant). Next, they choose one of five spacecraft chassis hulls—ranging from a lightweight CubeSat to a Heavy Flagship—and equip subsystems such as high-efficiency solar arrays, radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs), deep-space high-gain dishes, thermal control units, magnetic radiation shielding, and planetary spectrometers.

Behind the scenes, our physics and engineering engine evaluates every design choice in real time against metrics sourced from the NASA Planetary Fact Sheet (Metric). Fuel requirements scale with real planetary escape velocities, solar panel output drops via the inverse-square law based on real stellar distances, and harsh environments trigger thermal or radiation constraints. Once all engineering warnings are resolved within budget and payload mass limits, players unlock the launch sequence and watch their spacecraft enter a 2D orbital simulation rendered on an HTML5 Canvas.

Benefits & Intended Impact
Space mission design involves complex, competing constraints that can be difficult for students and beginners to visualize from textbooks alone. Cosmic Sandbox turns real aerospace trade-offs—such as deciding between heavy solar arrays versus nuclear RTGs for outer-system ice worlds—into an intuitive, hands-on sandbox. Our intended impact is to make STEM and planetary science accessible, engaging, and memorable for students, educators, and space enthusiasts worldwide.
